idiom_name: p-limit(concurrency) wrapping each task in a promise
implementation_notes: The main thread of a JavaScript runtime cannot block, so the classic blocking acquire has no meaning: the idiom is a promise-returning limiter - p-limit(concurrency) wraps each task and runs at most N at a time, queueing the rest and exposing activeCount/pendingCount - and the permit counter is replaced by the limiter's internal queue. For an explicit semaphore object with weights, priorities and cancellation, async-mutex's Semaphore provides acquire()/release()/runExclusive(); reach for the object form when the code needs to hold a permit across several awaits rather than around one task.
pitfalls: Calling the same limiter from inside a task it is already limiting deadlocks the queue; nested work needs a separate limiter.
clearQueue() leaves pending promises unresolved unless rejectOnClear is enabled, so callers awaiting them can hang forever.
A limiter is per-process and per-module instance: two bundled copies of the package give two independent counters for the same resource.

variants.name: Blocking semaphore over SharedArrayBuffer in a worker
variants.idiom_name: Atomics.wait / Atomics.notify on an Int32Array over a SharedArrayBuffer
variants.implementation_notes: Inside worker_threads a real blocking semaphore can be built from shared memory: an Int32Array over a SharedArrayBuffer holds the permit count, acquisition loops with Atomics.wait (or Atomics.waitAsync on the main thread) until a compare-exchange succeeds, and release uses Atomics.add plus Atomics.notify. This is the only place JavaScript has a blocking acquire - Atomics.wait throws on the main thread - so it belongs to worker-side hand-off between threads, not to ordinary application code.
pitfalls: Atomics.wait throws a TypeError on the main thread and on any thread that cannot be blocked; only workers may use the blocking form.
A spurious wakeup or a stolen notify is normal: the acquisition must re-read the counter in a loop rather than assume the permit is available.
SharedArrayBuffer requires cross-origin isolation in browsers, so the worker-semaphore form is often unavailable on the web platform.
